content.title: About
content.content: Pickled ginger root is thinly sliced fresh ginger that has been cured in a vinegar brine with sugar, salt and spices. It has a bright aroma, a mildly sweet‑sour taste and a crunchy texture. It is commonly used in Asian cuisine, especially with sushi, rolls, salads and as a garnish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pickled ginger, known as “gari” in Japan, is traditionally served with sushi to cleanse the palate between different pieces.
Ginger contains gingerol, the compound responsible for its characteristic pungent flavor and anti‑inflammatory properties.
The Japanese word “gari” literally means “pickled ginger”.
Pickling extends the shelf life of ginger, allowing it to retain its flavor and crunch for several months.
Ginger has been used in traditional medicine worldwide as a remedy for nausea and colds.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ginger stimulates gastric secretions and speeds up digestion, helping to reduce bloating.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory effect
items.content: Gingerol and shogaol exhibit anti‑inflammatory activity, which may help lessen joint discomfort.

items.title: Reduces nausea
items.content: Ginger is widely used to alleviate nausea, including motion sickness and morning sickness.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Phenolic compounds in ginger combat free radicals, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: B‑vitamins and vitamin C in ginger contribute to a stronger immune system.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to ginger, manifested as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of ginger can cause heartburn or irritation of the stomach lining in people with high acidity.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Ginger may enhance the effects of anticoagulants such as warfarin, so intake should be limited when using these medications.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pickled ginger is served in small portions alongside sushi, rolls, salads or as a snack. It can be added to Asian sauces, marinades, rice salads, or used as a fragrant garnish for fish and seafood dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep pickled ginger in a sealed jar in the refrigerator. When stored properly it retains its flavor and crunch for up to 6 months. Discard if you notice mold, discoloration or an off‑smell.
